data.title: Weekly Gains Hold Up Despite a Friday Slide as Chips Lead and Yields Climb
data.description:
VANCOUVER, BC, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Stock Preachers News Commentary - Wall Street closed out a volatile week with every major index still higher versus last Friday, even after a broad Friday retreat. The Nasdaq Composite led decliners with a 1.24% drop on the session, while the S&P 500 fell 0.75% and the Dow slipped 0.14%. For the week, the S&P 500 gained 2.15%, the Nasdaq rose 1.92% and the Dow added 1.83%, as chip-driven strength carried the market even as Friday gave back some ground heading into the weekend. Active Companies from around the markets with current developments this week include: Eli Lilly and Company ( LLY ) , vVardis , NVIDIA Corporation ( NVDA ) , Caterpillar Inc. ( CAT ) , and Bank of America Corporation ( BAC ) .

The S&P 500 closed at 7535.72, down 56.68 points on the day but up 158.86 points, or 2.15%, from last Friday's 7376.86 close. The index touched a week high of 7652.76 and a week low of 7422.24, and sits up 10.08% year to date. Its RSI14 reading of 45.6 points to a market that cooled off from overbought conditions during the week.

The Nasdaq Composite fell 315.80 points, or 1.24%, on Friday to 25050.29, trimming its weekly gain to 1.92% from the November 6 close of 24579.43. The index ranged between 24762.57 and 25649.85 during the week and carries an RSI14 of 41.6, the weakest among major indices. The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 75.29 points to 52221.80, still up 1.83% on the week and 8.65% year to date, while the Russell 2000 eased 17.98 points to 2781.08, up 0.98% for the week.

The VIX rose 1.14 points to 19.84 on Friday, essentially flat on the week, while the VXN volatility gauge climbed 1.33 points to 29.88 but ended the week down 4.14 points. The 10-year Treasury yield rose 3 basis points on the day and 27 basis points on the week to 5.13%. Gold fell 5.56% for the week to $3,885.70 an ounce, silver dropped 6.66% to $49.06, and WTI crude added 1.92% to $88.52 a barrel.

In other industry developments and happenings in the market this week include:

Eli Lilly and Company ( LLY ) Eli Lilly ( LLY ) broke ground on a $3.5 billion manufacturing facility in Pennsylvania's Lehigh Valley, part of its $50 billion push to expand U.S. medicine production. The site will manufacture injectable obesity medicines, including the investigational triple hormone receptor agonist retatrutide, and is expected to be operational by 2031.

The complaint alleges Nvidia ( NVDA ) made false or misleading statements related to its relationship with Megaspeed, a company suspected of helping China evade export controls, and that these circumstances raised national security concerns with potential reputational and business risk.

Explaining the top ranking, the outlet added that "its two agent modes plus a standalone validation layer prove which flaws attackers can exploit across web and API."

They cover web applications and APIs today, with cloud infrastructure testing on the roadmap. Astra Security pairs that continuous coverage with human-led penetration testing for high-context scenarios, an approach built to augment expert pentesters rather than replace them.

The CIO Times ranking follows Astra Security's recognition as the best autonomous pentesting tool for 2026 by HackerNoon in September. data.title: BofA Raises Server CPU Market Outlook on Agentic AI Demand, Chip Supply Visibility
data.description:
03:51 PM EST, 11/13/2026 (MT Newswires) -- Growing demand for agentic artificial intelligence and greater supply visibility should help boost the total addressable market for server central processing units by 2030, BofA Securities said.

The Wall Street giant now expects the server CPU TAM to expand to more than $240 billion by 2030 from about $210 billion projected previously, reflecting a compound annual growth rate of 39%, based on an estimated $64 billion for this year.

"Despite potential concerns around AI (capital expenditure) slowdown from (2028) onward, we flag AI compute demand is at all-time-high levels, and agentic adoption remains at nascent, low levels," BofA analyst Vivek Arya said in a note to clients e-mailed Thursday.

Recently, Morgan Stanley said the Democratic Party's decisive victory in the recent US midterm elections could weigh on broad AI sentiment amid expectations for increased restrictions on data center buildouts.

AI demand should sustain elevated server CPU volumes and average selling prices over time, BofA said. The brokerage's long-term TAM outlook factors in a stable single-digit growth in traditional CPUs to around $30 billion and more than $105 billion each for head-node compute and inference, and new agentic orchestration, respectively.

BofA raised its price objective on the Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) stock to $700 from $650, citing post-earnings AI clarity and a stronger long-term market outlook. The company is a "top CPU pick," driven by a wide portfolio, along with leadership in frequency and core/thread count, according to the note.

Earlier in November, AMD issued a stronger-than-expected fourth-quarter revenue outlook as third-quarter results topped the Street's estimates, driven by strength in its data center business.

BofA lowered its price objective for Intel ( INTC ) to $80 from $100, saying that limited clarity around the chipmaker's fourth-quarter and 2027 CPU supply outlook outweighs the potential upside from its foundry business.

Arm (ARM) continues to be the fastest market share gainer, while Qualcomm's ( QCOM ) CPU visibility is "limited, given multiple competition at key customers," BofA said.

The brokerage reduced its price objective on Nvidia's ( NVDA ) shares to $280 from $350, saying that despite its leadership in full-stack system driving Vera CPU ramp, the chipmaking giant faces higher near-term volatility.

Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive and a board member of Nvidia ( NVDA ) Thursday following reports that he had multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

In a note e-mailed Friday, Truist Securities said Nvidia's ( NVDA ) growth prospects could be constrained due to potential "know your customer" regulation following the controversy that led to Huang's ouster

The company is scheduled to release its latest quarterly results Tuesday.

data.title: Microsoft's global outage eases after disrupting businesses, governments for nearly a day
data.description:
Nov 13 (Reuters) - A global outage of Microsoft Outlook and Teams was easing on Friday after more than 24 hours of disruption crippled online communications across businesses and governments, though the company said it still had no timeline for full recovery of services.

Microsoft ( MSFT ) said server issues were behind the incident that also affected its Copilot AI assistant and that a broader rollout of software fixes was stabilizing the system. It said it was not aware of any malicious activity and ruled out AI as the cause. 

Outlook and Teams are two of the most widely used workplace applications with hundreds of millions of users. The outage prevented people from performing essential functions such as sending emails, managing calendars and hosting virtual meetings.

It affected government agencies from Australia and Japan to the United States, caused delays at trading firms, hindered some companies from publishing earnings and prompted airlines to warn customers of communication lags, according to public statements.

Organizations that host Microsoft ( MSFT ) services on their own servers, rather than in the cloud, were somewhat spared. 

ANOTHER OUTAGE FOR MICROSOFT 

The outage, reports of which started climbing around 1725 GMT on Thursday according to Ookla, is one of the longest in Microsoft's ( MSFT ) history and the second disruption to its services this year.

Microsoft ( MSFT ) said the outage specifically hit features tied to Exchange Online - its cloud-based email and scheduling hub - leaving unconnected applications operational.

The incident deepens questions about the global reliance on a handful of Big Tech companies that supply both the essential software and the cloud infrastructure that underpins it. 

It also highlighted the dependence on Microsoft's ( MSFT ) workplace software, with outage reports spiking as employees began their workdays across Asia and Europe, according to Downdetector's parent company, Ookla.

Downdetector logged more than 7.4 million reports worldwide, peaking at nearly 20,000 a minute, more than 1,500 times normal levels.

"It shows how much of the working day now runs through one provider's email and collaboration tools," said Luke Kehoe, lead industry analyst at Ookla.

Microsoft ( MSFT ) shares closed flat at $523.88 on Friday. The stock has gained roughly 8% so far this year.

Disruptions and financial losses from the outage could result in numerous insurance claims, but the overall hit to insurers is expected to be limited, said Mario De Cicco, vice president of European financial institutions at Morningstar DBRS.

De Cicco estimated global insured losses from the incident at between $300 million and $500 million, well below the $400 million to $1.5 billion financial toll from the 2024 CrowdStrike outage that crashed more than 8 million Windows-based computers and caused widespread disruptions.

Microsoft ( MSFT ) also faced an outage with its 365 services in January this year and in October last year. Last month, it reported an outage of its Azure cloud platform that impacted its suite of productivity software and a range of industries worldwide.

"The bigger worry is that this is not the first Microsoft ( MSFT ) 365 outage this year," said Josh Gilbert, a market analyst at trading platform eToro. 

"If reliability starts to look like a recurring problem, it hands every IT department a reason to think twice before putting even more of their business in one provider's hands." 

Still, some analysts have questioned whether such incidents can push customers on to rivals due to the steep switching costs of replacing tools embedded so deeply in daily operations. 

TRADES HAD TO BE CONFIRMED BY FAX

A spokesperson for the UK government said it was working with Microsoft ( MSFT ) to find a solution for the outage that hit organizations such as the NHS and London's Metropolitan Police.

Lack of access to emails and other services was impacting the Metropolitan Police's ability to report some crimes online, though its ability to respond to calls was not affected.

The NHS said its local services were turning to alternate measures such as using IT systems or paper records. 

For businesses, the fallout was widespread. 

European exchange operator Euronext reported email disruptions, British insurer Aviva activated backups for its earnings calls and Danish shipping giant Maersk warned customers of delayed updates.

American AI giants OpenAI and Anthropic also faced issues with Microsoft ( MSFT ) connectors, while Indian airlines IndiGo, Akasa Air and Air India said their email support services were impacted.

The outage also disrupted fund management at Taiwanese securities firms, life insurers, and investment trust companies. One of the companies went as far as cancelling a bond repurchase transaction, a source familiar with the situation told Reuters.

Another Taiwanese financial company resorted to using fax to confirm trades, a second source said.

In the US, electric truck maker Workhorse Group rescheduled its results on Thursday to November 16, while Switzerland's Richemont briefly delayed its first-half results announcement on Friday.

In Australia, where the spy agency and federal police were among organizations caught in the outage, Cyber Security Minister Tony Burke said Microsoft ( MSFT ) does not suspect a cyberattack.

"The impact that they are dealing with ... is very much on email systems," the minister added.

data.title: Investview, Inc. Reports Third-Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Strategic Business Update
data.description:

( INVU ) (the “Company”) today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, and provided an update on operating activity during the quarter. The quarter reflected a continued contraction in the Company's marketing network, a 10% increase in revenue from its health, beauty, and wellness businesses versus the second quarter of 2026, and continued investment in pre-commercial operations. Net income for the quarter was $9.0 million versus a $3.2 million loss in the second quarter of 2026, primarily attributable to the sale of the Company’s equity investment in an early-stage nuclear power and infrastructure technology company. The sale generated $10.8 million in net cash proceeds, strengthening the Company's financial position while its operating businesses continued to face challenges. Management will continue to focus on simplifying the portfolio, strengthening capital-allocation discipline, and clarifying the roles of its operating businesses, including selective commercial integration among Conectiv, MyLife Wellness, and Renu Laboratories.

Summary Consolidated Financial Highlights

Results of Operations — Three Months Ended September 30, 2026 vs. September 30, 2025

  • Gross Revenue (a Non-GAAP measure) decreased 72.6% to $2.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $8.6 million for the comparable prior-year period.
  • Net Revenue decreased 72.5% to $2.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $8.1 million for the comparable prior-year period.
  • Net cash used in operating activities was $1.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to net cash provided by operating activities of $0.6 million for the comparable prior-year period.
  • Loss from Operations (excluding discontinued operations) was $2.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $0.7 million for the comparable prior-year period.
  • Net Income increased $9.8 million to $9.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to a $0.8 million Net Loss for the comparable prior-year period. The increase was mainly due to the sale of the Company’s equity investments in an early-stage company focused on developing next-generation nuclear power and infrastructure technology.

Results of Operations — Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026 vs. September 30, 2025

  • Gross Revenue (a Non-GAAP measure) decreased 70.0% to $8.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $28.0 million for the comparable prior-year period.
  • Net Revenue decreased 69.6% to $8.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $26.5 million for the comparable prior-year period.
  • Net cash used in operating activities was $7.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to net cash used in operating activities of $3.1 million for the comparable prior-year period.
  • Loss from Operations (excluding discontinued operations) was $6.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $38.3 thousand for the comparable prior-year period.
  • Net Income increased $3.0 million to $1.9 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to a $1.1 million Net Loss for the comparable prior-year period. The increase was mainly due to the sale of the Company’s equity investments in an early-stage company focused on developing next-generation nuclear power and infrastructure technology.

Balance Sheet Data — September 30, 2026 vs. December 31, 2025

  • Cash, cash equivalents and digital assets increased 20.4% to $18.6 million at September 30, 2026, an increase of $3.2 million from $15.5 million at December 31, 2025. The increase was primarily attributable to $10.8 million in net cash proceeds from the sale of the Company’s equity investment in an early-stage company developing next-generation nuclear power and infrastructure technology, partially offset by $7.1 million in net cash used in operating activities.
  • Total assets increased $0.5 million, or 2.5%, to $22.0 million. Total liabilities decreased $0.9 million, or 7.2%, to $11.7 million. The Company's current ratio increased 33% to 2.83 as of September 30, 2026.
  • Working capital increased $2.7 million, or 39.4%, as of September 30, 2026, compared to December 31, 2025, excluding $5.7 million in liquid digital assets held at quarter-end.
  • Outstanding debt increased by $0.3 million to $3.9 million at September 30, 2026, up from $3.6 million at December 31, 2025.
  • Total stockholders' equity was $10.4 million at September 30, 2026, an increase of $1.5 million, or 16.3%, from $8.9 million at December 31, 2025. During the third quarter, the Company repurchased 1,958,841 shares of its common stock under its authorized stock repurchase program at an average price of $0.0182 per share, representing a 0.11% reduction in common shares outstanding. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company repurchased a total of 4,821,883 shares at an average price of $0.0219 per share, representing a cumulative 0.26% reduction in common shares outstanding.

Portfolio Company and Strategic Review

Direct-to-Consumer Marketing Platform — Conectiv

Conectiv net revenue was $1.8 million in the third quarter of 2026, a decrease of $5.2 million, or 74.1%, compared to the prior-year period. The decline primarily reflected continued contraction in the Company's European marketing network following the December 2025 UOKiK administrative decision in Poland. The Company has appealed the decision, which remains pending, and continues to operate in European Union markets under its applicable compliance procedures.

During 2026, Conectiv continued its strategic transition from a financial education-focused platform to an integrated Finance + Wellness + Lifestyle membership offering. The expanded model combines financial education and tools with MyLife Wellness products, travel and lifestyle benefits, live events, and community engagement, supported by subscription-based memberships and recurring product replenishment programs. In this model, Conectiv provides the membership and distributor infrastructure, MyLife Wellness markets consumer health and wellness products, and Renu Laboratories provides product development and manufacturing capabilities.

During the third quarter, Conectiv introduced Coneqtx, a new mobile trading education application providing access to an expanded library of financial education content, trading tools, market research, and analysis. The application is intended to enhance the member experience and support engagement and retention.

Conectiv also expanded its distribution network through the addition of two selling organizations during 2026 and continued advancing its omnichannel sales and marketing strategy, integrating independent distributors with direct-to-consumer digital marketing, social media, influencer partnerships, and live events to broaden customer reach and support membership growth.

Although management expects that in the long-term the operational initiatives it has implemented during 2026 will improve Connectiv’s results of operation, to date, these initiatives have not yet produced an increase in sales sufficient to offset the decline in Connectiv’s European and other operations. Despite these headwinds, management remains focused, however, on strengthening member engagement and retention, developing additional recurring revenue streams, and improving operating performance through its expanded membership offerings and integrated sales and marketing initiatives.

Health, Beauty, and Wellness Products

The Health, Beauty, and Wellness Products segment, which entails the financial results of Renu Laboratories and MyLife Wellness, generated net revenue of $0.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $1.1 million for the same period in 2025 — a decrease of $0.6 million, or 59.3%.

Renu Laboratories

Renu Laboratories, the Company's U.S.-based, FDA-registered contract manufacturer of skincare, haircare, body care, and wellness products, continued to implement a strategic shift toward higher-margin customer relationships and more profitable manufacturing opportunities. As part of this transition, management discontinued or restructured certain higher-volume, lower-margin customer arrangements, contributing to lower revenue during the quarter while positioning the business to pursue opportunities with more favorable margin characteristics.

The Company continues to pursue new customer opportunities and expanded relationships with existing customers. It is also pursuing targeted investments in business development, marketing, manufacturing capabilities, production technology, and key personnel, while evaluating potential strategic business combinations to support customer acquisition, production efficiency, and longer-term growth. Despite the continued contraction in the Renu business, management remains focused on rebuilding manufacturing volume and strengthening operating performance, while evaluating the business based on revenue performance, customer profitability, operating costs, and capital requirements.

MyLife Wellness  

MyLife Wellness ("MLW"), the Company's consumer health and wellness brand, leverages Renu Laboratories' product development and manufacturing capabilities alongside Conectiv's technology, membership, and distributor infrastructure. Its product portfolio includes supplements supporting gut, metabolic, cognitive, and sleep health, functional coffee, pain relief and recovery products, and facial-care offerings, distributed through e-commerce and the Company's distributor network.

The Company continues to strengthen its direct-to-consumer marketing initiatives, digital and social media presence, influencer partnerships, and distributor engagement to broaden brand awareness and customer reach. Management remains focused on expanding recurring product sales and repeat customer purchasing through its product portfolio and distribution channels.

Financial Services Initiatives

Opencash Securities — Development and Commercialization Update

During the third quarter of 2026, the Company continued to advance the development and commercialization efforts of Opencash Securities LLC (“Opencash”), its registered broker-dealer and digital brokerage platform.

Although not yet ready for commercial application, the platform is being developed to support trading in equities, exchange-traded funds (“ETFs”), equity options, and mutual funds. The Company intends to introduce two complementary offerings for self-directed retail investors: Opencash, a mobile application designed for emerging and experienced investors seeking accessible and intuitive trading capabilities, and OpencashPro, a web-based platform tailored to active and more experienced traders seeking advanced market data, analytical tools, and expanded trading functionality.

The Company is targeting initial commercial operations by the end of the second quarter of 2027, with a phased expansion of platform capabilities and services anticipated through the remainder of 2027 and into 2028. Launch timing and platform capabilities remain subject to applicable regulatory requirements, third-party capabilities, and operational and technological readiness; no definitive launch date has been established. As of September 30, 2026, Opencash remained pre-commercial and pre-revenue, with the Company continuing to incur related development and operating expenses.

Although during the quarter our net revenue declined to $2.2 million, and we reported an operating loss (excluding discontinued operations) of $2.1 million, and net income of $9.0 million, we also significantly enhanced our liquidity as we sold for $10.8 million our equity investment in an early-stage nuclear power and infrastructure technology company. data.title: AI-NATIVE SOFTWARE COMPANIES LEAD ON GROWTH, BUT STRONGER ECONOMICS HAVE NOT YET FOLLOWED
data.description:
17th annual benchmark from KeyBanc Capital Markets, formerly the SaaS Survey, expands to measure how AI is reshaping the private software industry

SAN FRANCISCO, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- KeyBanc Capital Markets Inc., the corporate and investment banking unit of KeyCorp ( KEY ) , today released results from its 17th annual AI x Software Benchmark, one of the longest-running benchmarks of financial and operating performance by software companies. Formerly known as the SaaS Survey, the benchmark has been expanded this year to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) is changing product strategy, monetization, unit economics, and operating models.

This year's findings show that companies selling AI as their primary product are growing significantly faster than their peers, but they also report weaker profitability and revenue productivity than software companies embedding AI into existing products. AI adoption is widespread; monetization and measurable financial impact remain early.

"For 17 years, this benchmark has given software operators and investors a clear view of how the industry is performing. This year, the central question is whether AI is creating a durable advantage," said Scott Peterson, Managing Director, Software Investment Banking at KeyBanc Capital Markets. " AI is accelerating growth and compressing development cycles, but AI spend is running ahead of budget and the economics are still catching up. 2026 is a proving year for AI-driven revenue."

"Developer headcount has historically been one of the biggest constraints for software development. AI coding tools are loosening that constraint as developer productivity improves," added Peterson. "But rather than let those gains drop to the bottom line, companies are reinvesting them to ship more product faster."

TOP TRENDS AND INSIGHTS:

AI-native companies lead on growth, while embedded AI leads on economics

  • Companies selling AI as their primary product reported median ARR growth of 34% in 2025, compared with 22% for companies embedding AI in broader products and 9% for companies still developing customer-facing AI.
  • Core AI product companies reported a median EBITDA margin of (12%) in 2025, compared with (1%) for embedded AI companies
  • Embedded AI companies also led on productivity, with ARR per FTE at $201K versus $117K for core AI product companies.
  • Companies that charge separately for AI products reported 27% median ARR growth in 2025, versus 17% for those that do not. That growth advantage has not yet translated into higher net retention.

AI revenue is small but poised to accelerate quickly

  • AI-driven ARR is projected to grow 128% in 2026, up from 74% in 2025, yet will still only represent 12% of total ARR.
  • Overall median ARR growth was 24% in 2025 and is projected at 23% in 2026, with participants planning for a broad-based acceleration to 40% in 2027.
  • Overall median EBITDA margin is expected to improve from (3%) in 2025 to 1% in 2026.

AI spend is outpacing budgets and showing up in margins before growth

  • More than four in 10 respondents (44%) report AI spend over budget year to date, and roughly a quarter (24%) are over by more than 20%. Higher-than-expected token usage was the most cited driver of variance.
  • Companies spending more than 5% of revenue on AI reported a median gross margin of 66% in 2025, compared with 78% for those spending less than 2%.

AI is speeding up product development, and workforce impact expected to broaden

  • 92% of respondents report that AI is shortening product development cycles, and 91% deploy AI internally in engineering.
  • 65% of participants report no AI-related headcount reduction or reallocation in 2025. Looking out 12 to 24 months, which falls to 34% with R&D (45%) and customer service (37%) the functions most likely to be affected.

Customers are building with AI, while autonomous agents remain early

  • 57% of respondents say their customers are building alternative products with AI coding tools.
  • Only 20% offer fully autonomous agents to their customers.

data.title: US STOCKS-Wall St slides as Nvidia uncertainty drags tech shares lower
data.description:
(Updates to afternoon trading, adds analyst comments)

* Microsoft ( MSFT ) edges up after global outage eases

* Nvidia ( NVDA ) falls further following Jensen Huang's exit

* Indexes down: Dow 0.01%, S&P 500 0.51%, Nasdaq 0.93%

By Chuck Mikolajczak and Niket Nishant

NEW YORK, Nov 13 (Reuters) - US stocks were lower on Friday, as concerns about Nvidia ( NVDA ) pressured technology shares, while a reading on inflation failed to alter expectations for more rate hikes from the Federal Reserve.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) shares fell 2.2% and were poised for their sixth straight week of declines, their longest streak since October 2012, after CEO Jensen Huang's resignation on Thursday, following revelations of his relationship with a businesswoman suspected by the US of spying for Beijing.

The Financial Times reported that Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board has approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential successor to Huang.

The uncertainty about leadership at the chipmaker has raised concerns about the durability of the AI trade, given Nvidia's ( NVDA ) primary role in the industry's boom and its financial ties to several companies in the sector, which has been a pillar of the bull market in equities.

"The tech trade, the AI trade, Nvidia ( NVDA ) is going to go through a period of volatility, and you're going to see the bulls and bears kind of wrestle on where this narrative goes through the rest of the year ... there's been a loss of confidence," said Anthony Saglimbene, chief market strategist at Ameriprise Financial in Troy, Michigan.

"The market and investors are trying to navigate what does the AI theme look like when we have the absence of Jensen Huang, who was basically the AI champion and willing to use Nvidia's ( NVDA ) balance sheet to fund a lot of this AI expansion. That's gone."

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 5.36 points, or 0.01%, to 52,291.73, the S&P 500 lost 38.87 points, or 0.51%, to 7,553.53 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 236.49 points, or 0.93%, to 25,129.60.

Despite the recent volatility, the major indexes were on track for weekly gains, with the Nasdaq and S&P 500 both set to snap a four-week streak of declines.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 3.7%, with Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) and Broadcom ( AVGO ) the biggest drags.

Neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius ( NBIS ) also slumped, while data center-related firms IREN ( IREN ) and Applied Digital ( APLD ) retreated as well.

The losses come ahead of AI company Anthropic's much-anticipated IPO next week, which could test investor appetite for established AI heavyweights as money potentially shifts toward the new entrant.

The S&P 500 technology index was off 1.6% as the worst-performing of the 11 major S&P sectors. But Microsoft ( MSFT ) shares edged up 0.4% after a global outage that included its Outlook and Teams products began to ease.

INFLATION CONCERNS REMAIN

On the economic front, the Labor Department said US producer prices were slightly cooler than expected in October, but still shot up 6.5% year over year, the largest annual gain since November 2022.

The data kept expectations for a rate hike of at least 25 basis points at the Fed's December meeting completely locked in, with markets pricing in a roughly 10% chance for an outsized 50-basis-point increase, according to CME FedWatch.

Comments from multiple Fed officials earlier this week suggested the US central bank was open to a more aggressive path of rate hikes as price pressures worsen.

data.title: Hassett expected to leave Trump administration, Semafor reports
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 13 (Reuters) - The White House denied on Friday that National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett was leaving the Trump administration in the coming weeks.

Earlier on Friday, Semafor, citing three people familiar with the plan, reported that Hassett was departing in the coming weeks and had been inquiring about roles outside the administration since before the Nov. 3 midterm elections, which resulted in Democrats retaking both chambers of the US Congress, delivering a blow for Republican President Donald Trump.

"There is no factual basis for this reporting. Kevin Hassett is a key member of President Trump's economic team and will continue working to advance President Trump's economic policies," a White House official said.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who could hold both roles, and his counselor, David Zervos, are among the people being eyed to replace Hassett, according to Semafor. The report said Hassett's plans could change.

Semafor said Hassett's departure would be the latest in a series of staffing changes at the White House. Last week, Trump replaced his chief of staff, Susie Wiles, with longtime aide Stephen Miller.

The US Treasury Department did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Hassett served as the chairman of the White House Council of Economic Advisers during Trump's first administration.

He left the role in 2019 but later returned to the White House to serve as a senior adviser to Trump during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Hassett was considered to replace Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell last year, but Kevin Warsh eventually got the role.

data.title: PRECIOUS-Rate-hike bets keep gold on track for worst week in four months
data.description:
* US PPI for final demand rose 0.3% last month

* Spot gold down about 4.5% this week, the most since early June

* Silver, platinum and palladium also head for weekly declines

(Updates prices for US closing hours)

By Anjana Anil

Nov 13 (Reuters) - Gold firmed on Friday as a largely in-line US inflation reading alleviated some bets on a bigger rate hike, but Thursday's selloff to a more-than-a-year low kept bullion on track for a weekly decline.

Spot gold ticked up 0.1% at $3,879.71 per ounce as of 2:05 p.m. ET (1905 GMT), after briefly touching a session high of $3,922.97 when the US Producer Price Index data came out.

US gold futures for December delivery settled largely unchanged at $3,886.30 per ounce.

The Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.3% last month, after an upwardly revised 1.4% surge in September, data showed on Friday. A Reuters poll had forecast PPI climbing 0.4%.

"Gold is struggling to hold initial gains from PPI as bond markets continue to struggle, confronted with Fed hawkishness," independent analyst Tai Wong said. "PPI didn't surprise high like last month, but core at 0.3% month-on-month remains too high for policymakers."

Gold prices slid 3% on Thursday, hitting a more-than-one-year low, as oil climbed, spurring fears of higher inflation and elevated interest rates. The fall was accentuated by hotter-than-expected Consumer Price Index data earlier this week.

Bullion has shed about 4.5% so far this week and is poised to log its worst week since early June.

"It's been a tough week for gold, which may struggle to retake 4,000 with Fed hawks out in force," Wong added.

Markets see a 91.4% chance of a 25-basis-point US rate hike in December, versus 96.2% before the PPI data. The probability of a larger 50-basis-point move, however, is now seen at 8.6%, below the 13.8% chance before PPI, according to CME's FedWatch Tool.

Higher interest rates tend to diminish non-yielding gold's appeal.

Among other metals, spot silver fell 1.9% to $49.05 per ounce, platinum fell 1.9% to $1,490.06, while palladium climbed 1.1% to $1,004.40.

All three metals were also on course to post losses for the week.

data.title: Pine AI Open-Sources an AI Filmmaking Studio and Brings Real-World Phone Calls to Pine Computer
data.description:
Weeks after launching its AI-native computer, Pine AI unveils new applications and capabilities built on the platform, starting with open-source filmmaking and autonomous phone calls.

SAN FRANCISCO, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Pine AI today released Pine Drama Studio, an open-source AI filmmaking studio built on Pine Computer. It also brought Pine Phone into Pine Computer, so AI agents can make real-world phone calls as part of their work.

The announcements mark Pine Computer's next step: from a computer built for AI to a platform for AI-native applications. Pine Computer drew about 24 million views on its Oct. 9 launch day. Developers in early access were already building on it, and production teams now use it for video creation and other long-running work. Pine Drama Studio shows that agents can run an entire creative production. Pine Phone takes them beyond software, into conversations with real businesses.

"Pine Drama shows what agents can create. Pine Phone shows how they can act in the real world," said Stanley Wei, co-founder and CEO of Pine AI. "We gave AI a computer. Now we're seeing what people can build with it."

Pine Drama Studio: agents run the production, creators direct it

Pine Drama Studio grew out of what developers built on Pine Computer. AI short-drama production was the first workload to take off, and professional teams brought the hardest requirement: whole series, not single clips.

One of those teams, an AI short-drama studio in Australia, moved its production onto Pine Drama Studio in October, after a September beta. Each member of its team used to produce 2 to 3 minutes of video a day. The same people now produce 30 to 50 minutes a day, with several episodes in production at once.

"We used to spend most of our time generating clips, fixing inconsistencies, and stitching everything together. With Pine Drama Studio, the same team can now produce 10 times more video while running multiple episodes in parallel." said Alec, CTO of an Australia-based AI short-drama production company.

Video models make remarkable clips, but a series means hundreds of shots that must stay consistent across episodes. In Pine Drama Studio, a producer starts with a screenplay and a single instruction. Agents then do the production work:

  • Build the story bible;
  • Design the characters, locations and props once for the whole series;
  • Storyboard and generate every shot;
  • Check the takes and redo what drifts;
  • Cut the approved takes into episodes.

Creators approve the designs, storyboards, takes and final cuts. Each episode runs on its own Pine Computer, so a whole series can be in production at once, and when something changes, agents regenerate only the affected shots.

  • Open source, and the studio's own. The Studio is free under Apache 2.0. Teams can change its code and the workflow in its plain skill files, choose their own models, and add their own steps, such as dubbing and localization. Projects and production know-how stay in the studio's own folder.
  • Pine runs the heavy work. Generation and the agents' work run on Pine Computers in the cloud. That cloud compute is the paid part.

Pine Phone: calling, built into the computer

Pine Phone makes the phone call a native capability of Pine Computer, not a separate voice assistant. An agent changing a booking in a browser may find that the last step needs a call. It phones the business, talks it through, and finishes the task, without switching apps.

People already using Muse or Instinct can connect them to Pine Phone. Pine Phone runs on Pine Voice 1.0, which ranks first on τ³-Voice (English) at 87.3% Pass@1.

Get started

  • Developers: Build on Pine Computer and give your agent a phone at pinecomputer.io. Explore the developer documentation.
  • Watch: The Pine Drama Studio and Pine Phone launch films.

Pine AI builds AI that gets real-world work done for people and businesses, across phone calls, websites, software and other digital systems. Its systems have handled millions of real-world tasks, where reliability, latency and permissions matter. Earlier in 2026, Pine Voice reached No. 1 on τ³-Voice, a benchmark from researchers at Sierra and Princeton that tests whether real-time voice AI can hold a conversation while completing real-world tasks. data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

data.title: US extends shipping law waiver 90 days, to allow freer movement of oil, commodities
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov 13 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump extended for 90 days a waiver of a shipping law to allow foreign-flagged ships to transport oil and other commodities between US ports, a White House official said on Friday.

Reuters reported on Thursday that industry sources said the administration would extend the waiver on the more than 100-year-old Jones Act. 

It has been the longest waiver in the history of the shipping law.

The administration issued a blanket waiver in March, a month after the US launched the war on Iran, in an effort to lower oil and fuel prices. In August, it extended the waiver but mandated that decisions would be made on a case-by-case basis, a stipulation continued through the latest waiver.  

The ⁠Jones Act requires cargo moving between US ports to be carried on ships built in the US, owned by US companies and crewed by American workers. Allowing the waiver aims to lower gas, diesel and fertilizer prices driven up by the war on Iran by increasing shipping flexibility and reducing transport bottlenecks.

Since the waiver was issued in March, an additional 90 million barrels of petroleum, mostly refined, have been shipped between US ports, the White House said. The total includes 27 million barrels of gasoline, 26 million barrels of crude oil, and 6 million barrels of renewable fuels.

The length of waivers has been limited in the past as the Jones Act is supported by the domestic shipbuilding business, a powerful lobby across the country.   

(Reporting by Timothy Gardner, Arathy Somasekhar and Jarrett Renshaw; Editing by Andrea Ricci)

data.title: Krach Institute for Tech Diplomacy at Purdue Launches the World's First Global Trusted Tech Standard (xGTT) with the Backing of Dozens of Visionary Leaders
data.description:
A free, open standard gives governments, businesses, universities and other decision-makers a common framework to assess whether companies operate in alignment with democratic values

WASHINGTON, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Krach Institute for Tech Diplomacy at Purdue today announced the launch of the Global Trusted Tech Standard (xGTT), the world's first open standard for trusted technology. The principle behind xGTT is straightforward: trust must be earned through conduct. In democratic markets, companies earn trust by respecting the laws, rights, and principles that underpin free societies. The xGTT Standard provides governments, businesses, universities, and other institutions with a common, evidence-based framework for assessing whether a company has earned that trust.

Unlike standards that narrowly focus on technical performance, xGTT goes one step further, covering companies' compatibility with democratic values, such as respect for the rule of law, human rights, intellectual property, transparency, accountability, and others. xGTT applies to 15 critical and emerging technology (CET) sectors that are central to economic competitiveness, national security, and democratic resilience. Its criteria draw on the laws, regulations, standards, and established practices of 18 technologically advanced democracies, providing a shared reference point grounded in multiple jurisdictions rather than the position of any single government.

15 CETs covered by xGTT

18 Techno-Democracies Anchoring xGTT Criteria

1. Advanced Communications & Networking
2. Advanced Computing
3. Advanced Manufacturing & Materials
4. Artificial Intelligence
5. Autonomous Systems & Robotics
6. Biotechnology
7. Cybersecurity & Data Security
8. Directed Energy
9. Energy Technologies
10. Human-Machine Interfaces & Neurotech
11. Hypersonics
12. Positioning, Navigation & Timing
13. Quantum Technologies
14. Semiconductors & Microelectronics
15. Space Technologies

1. Australia
2. Canada
3. Denmark
4. Estonia
5. Finland
6. France
7. Germany
8. India
9. Israel
10. Japan
11. Netherlands
12. New Zealand

16. Taiwan
17. United Kingdom
18. United States 

The Global Trusted Tech Standard (xGTT) was announced at the Krach Institute for Tech Diplomacy at Purdue's 2026 Trusted Tech Summit, the premier forum for Tech Diplomancy. The annual Summit brings together U.S. and allied government officials, technology executives, investors, and strategic partners to address the alliances, standards, and strategies shaping trusted technology. The launch of xGTT advances that mission by providing a shared, evidence-based framework for assessing corporate trustworthiness across critical and emerging technology sectors.

"Technology will either serve humanity or be used to undermine it, and trust is a decisive factor. By grounding economic collaboration in democratic principles, the Global Trusted Tech Standard makes it easier to operate efficiently in the free world, giving companies that earn trust a real competitive advantage," said Keith Krach, Chairman of the Krach Institute for Tech Diplomacy at Purdue. "Together, we can ensure tomorrow's technology advances freedom for generations to come."

"Trust is the free world's superpower, and it is how we set the pace," said Michelle Giuda, CEO of the Krach Institute. "The Global Trusted Tech Standard delivers a real-world definition of trusted technology. It's simple, open, and free. Governments, companies, and universities can use it to guide procurement, supply chains, partnerships, and research, so collaboration moves faster and security and prosperity grow. That is how we win against those who weaponize technology against people."

xGTT Board of Governors

The xGTT Standard is guided by a Board of Governors, comprising 20 distinguished international experts spanning government, industry, academia, and civil society across 9 countries:

  • Audrey Tang, Chair of the xGTT Board; Taiwan's Cyber Ambassador-at-Large
  • Roberto Baldoni, former Deputy Director General of Italian Intelligence; founding Director General of Italy's National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN)
  • Isabel Cane, former Head of OECD Trust in Business and Blue Dot Network
  • Alex Capri, Senior Fellow and Lecturer, NUS Business School in Singapore
  • Dan DeLaurentis, Professor of Aeronautics and Astronautics and EVP for Research, Purdue University
  • Mike Derrios, Executive Director, Greg and Camille Baroni Center for Government Contracting, George Mason University
  • Rick Echevarria, Senior Vice President of Business Development, Keyfactor
  • Obiageli "Oby" Ezekwesili, former Nigerian Minister of Education and of Minerals; former World Bank Vice President for Africa
  • Fernando Garibay, GRAMMY® and BMI award-winning producer, songwriter, entrepreneur, author; Chairman and CEO, The Garibay Institute
  • Melanie Garson, Associate Professor in International Security, University College London
  • Dan Goldin, former Administrator, NASA
  • Yasmin Green, CEO, Jigsaw
  • Takashi Oda, Director of Business Strategy, NTT
  • Roman Pačka, Chief Advisor to the Director of the Czech National Cyber and Information Security Agency (NÚKIB)
  • Heather Petersen, former Head of Trust Strategy, DocuSign; former Executive Director, xDTM Standard Association
  • David Roberts, Executive Director, Li-Bridge
  • Harsh Shringla, Member of Parliament; former Indian Ambassador to the U.S.
  • Tom Sonderman, CEO, SkyWater Technology
  • Yigal Unna, former Director General, Israel's National Cyber Directorate
  • Ken Urquhart, Senior Fellow at the Krach Institute for Tech Diplomacy at Purdue

The Board reviews the criteria on a standing basis, so the xGTT Standard adapts as the underlying technologies, and the risks they carry, continue to evolve. xGTT is guided by people who understand how real-world technology decisions are made. Their experience helps keep it relevant to the people and institutions that will use it.

How xGTT Works

The xGTT Standard contains 31 criteria for assessing a company's trustworthiness. These include 10 Red-Line Disqualifiers and 21 additional criteria covering Four Dimensions of Trust:

  • Democratic Government Trust: Whether democratic governments have trusted the company enough to contract with it, vet it, or invest in it.
  • Legal & Regulatory Compliance: Whether the company is free of serious misconduct findings by courts or governments that it has not remedied, such as corruption, fraud, repeated privacy violations, or intellectual property infringement.
  • Transparency & Disclosures: Whether the company's practices are open to independent verification, including audited financials, transparency about government requests for data, democratic supply chain practices, and published policies on corruption, human rights, and whistleblowers.
  • Technical Security Practices: Whether the company protects and manages its technology responsibly, from cybersecurity and secure software development to privacy, responsible AI, export controls, environmental compliance, and operational resilience.

A confirmed Red-Line failure disqualifies a company and ends the evaluation. For all other criteria, each applicable criterion receives a verdict of PASS, FAIL, UNCLEAR, or N/A, depending on the available evidence and whether the criterion applies. xGTT does not produce a single overall score or rank companies against one another.

Who xGTT is Designed For

xGTT helps a broad range of leaders make faster, evidence-based decisions about the trustworthiness of companies they may buy from, invest in, or partner with. Its criteria cover both technological excellence and democratic values, and each user applies them under its own authority and for its own purposes:

  • Governments and procurement authorities can integrate xGTT into procurement rules, requests for proposals (RFPs), and supply-chain vetting.
  • Defense forces can integrate it into military RFPs, procurement rules, and vetting of dual-use supply chains.
  • Enterprises and investors can apply it to enhance vendor due diligence, supply-chain risk assessment, and partnership decisions.
  • Industry associations and manufacturers can use it to demonstrate supplier trustworthiness, strengthen integration into global value chains, and expand access to trusted international markets.
  • Universities, research institutions, and standards bodies can use it as a reference for policy development, academic research, and coordination among like-minded institutions.

The xGTT Standard is for informational use only. It is not investment, legal, or financial advice, and xGTT evaluations do not constitute recommendations for or against any company, are not a regulatory finding or legal determination, and are not a substitute for independent due diligence. All decisions remain the responsibility of the organizations that use xGTT.

Government, Industry, and Civil Society Leaders Support the xGTT Standard

The Krach Institute already has endorsements from individuals all over the globe to include individuals from the Special Competitive Studies Project, Australian Strategic Policy Institute, Abba Eban Institute for Diplomacy and Foreign Relations, EDGE AI Foundation, Secure Economic Ecosystem, George Mason University's Baroni Center for Government Contracting, Keyfactor, Leonardo US Corporation, Jigsaw, U.S.-Taiwan Business Council, Mahindra Group, ReElement Africa, ADASA Inc., SEMI Americas, Opportunity International, Guidehouse, and TalentCraft. The standard also has the backing of representatives from the governments of the Czech Republic, Estonia, India, Israel, Italy, Panama, Romania, Taiwan and Ukraine, reflecting a growing commitment among democratic partners to advance trusted technology grounded in shared values.

If we all do not understand this simple statement and we do not work to implement it inside our regular and normal activities, within the institutions and industries, we have lost a great opportunity to build a strong and free society. data.title: Nvidia's Huang turns to Paul Weiss, law firm that inked deal with Trump
data.description:
* Jensen Huang turned to New York firm amid ouster

* Paul Weiss faced Trump executive order before White House deal

* Leader Brad Karp resigned as chair over Epstein communications

By Mike Scarcella

WASHINGTON, Nov 13 (Reuters) - Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang turned to law firm Paul Weiss amid his rapid fall this week, tapping a firm that reached a controversial deal with President Donald Trump last year and whose own longtime leader was forced to step down in February.

Huang resigned on Thursday after more than 30 years leading the top AI chipmaker, following reports that he had extramarital affairs with three women, including an Nvidia ( NVDA ) executive and Chinese businesswoman whom US intelligence suspects of being ​a Chinese spy.

Paul Weiss, Nvidia ( NVDA ) and a spokesperson for Huang had no immediate comment on Friday about the nature of the law firm's work for Huang.

New-York based Paul Weiss, with more than 1,500 lawyers, long has been a go-to for corporate boards and executives facing regulatory scrutiny, misconduct allegations or other reputational crises.

It built a reputation pairing lucrative work for Citigroup and other business clients with liberal advocacy and fundraising for Democratic candidates, including Kamala Harris.

But the firm drew sharp criticism within the legal profession and from Democrats last year after striking a deal with Trump to rescind an executive order the Republican president issued against it in March 2025.

Trump's order suspended security clearances for the firm's lawyers and restricted their access to government buildings and officials, citing its internal diversity policies and its association with a prosecutor who investigated the president.

Paul Weiss pledged in its settlement to dedicate $40 million in pro bono legal services to support "mutually agreed" projects with the White House, sparking similar deals by eight other law firms. Its longtime chairman Brad Karp defended the accord, calling Trump's order an existential threat.

The tumult facing Karp ramped up early this year, after emails surfaced showing Karp's extensive personal and business communications with the late convicted sex offender and financier Jeffrey Epstein.

Karp resigned from his leadership post in February, saying the reports about Epstein had created a distraction that was not in the firm's interests. He has not been accused of wrongdoing.

GO-TO FIRM FOR CORPORATE CRISES

Paul Weiss has a stable of former senior Justice Department officials and others who frequently step in for clients when crisis strikes.

BlackRock in 2021 hired partner Loretta Lynch, who was US Attorney General under President Barack Obama, to assist with an internal probe of former employees' claims of sexual harassment and discrimination.

Huang is working with Paul Weiss partners Melinda Haag and Walter Brown, the New York Times reported on Thursday. Haag served as US attorney in San Francisco during the Obama administration. She and Brown did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Reuters could not independently confirm which lawyers at the firm are representing Huang.

The Republican leaders of several US House committees, including Foreign Affairs, addressed a letter to Brown on Thursday stating they wish to interview Huang in closed-door session next month.

Haag successfully defended former Fitbit executive Katherine Mogal, who was acquitted in 2020 of federal charges alleging theft of trade secrets from a rival wearable-device maker. Brown is on the team defending Meta Platforms in a lawsuit by an Australian mining magnate over scam ads on Facebook showing him promoting fake cryptocurrency.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) board has hired another top firm, Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Kratz to conduct an independent investigation. That probe will be led by Wachtell's Joon Kim, a former senior federal prosecutor in Manhattan.

(Reporting by Mike Scarcella; additional reporting by Alexandra Alper. Editing by David Bario and Nick Zieminski)
